entries.decision: Overgoal pivot: transform ZCode into ZBill, a Windows-first desktop app for creating bill reports; keep the agent-chat core, expand bill features (any bill type, item review/edit, report history/archive, more outputs), and hard-delete most non-billing ZCode design and features from the codebase.
entries.provenance: Repo owner directive in ADE chat session 10e5b846: 'the overgoal i want to transform zcode to not be zcode at all. it should be app for create bill report as i want but it need more than what feature is now. it also need to cut down most of design and feature of zcode', plus four structured scope answers (features/shell/cut/platform), 2026-11-09.

entries.decision: Adopt the zbill/m1-scaffold product work by PORTING its product bits onto main (38 files: ZBill product mode defines, sidebar entry hiding, dev-task env, zbill-billing pipeline + fixtures, Google-plugins M2 scope record, ZBILL-M1 history) instead of merging the branch; branch keeps the stale vendored kit copies and remains the historical record.
entries.provenance: Agent decision within owner-confirmed pivot direction, 2026-11-09; overlap analysis showed 855+ vendored .super-speckit files changed on both sides since fork point a9fe401e, making a raw merge conflict-heavy with no product value.
entries.rationale: Main's kit, gates, and journey config are strictly newer (filled lint/format/unit gates, journey-ux executor config); the scaffold's copies predate them. Port avoids regressing verification infrastructure while preserving every ZBill product artifact.
consequences: zbill-billing/ and ZBill product mode now exist on main; typecheck clean, lint 0 errors after port
Branch zbill/m1-scaffold is retained unmerged as provenance; do not delete without owner approval
Ported packages/shared/package.json keeps a trailing newline (fmt convention) unlike the branch copy

entries.decision: Cut execution order: wave 1 removes coding-plan purchase panels, plugin marketplace, and automations surfaces; wave 2 removes remote-connection device management (SSH/WSL/Docker) and web/mobile remote-control modules; each wave is a verified slice (code + routes + docs + checks) with its import-graph investigation completed first (receipt steps S4/S5).
